en-US.description: Spec-first continuity framework for AI-assisted development
en-US.longDescription: Anchors ties spec, feature and test together through a shared identity code, then confronts each artifact against the rules declared in anchors.yaml. It maps the project as a graph, propagates change from the anchor outward, and gates every step — so work guided by AI stays anchored to what was decided.
en-US.name: Anchors
en-US.releaseNotes:
v0.1.405
- New gate symbol-exists: a name marked as a symbol is in the project's code. A comment or a spec marks the names it cites with @@name, #name or $name (dotted parts too: #Reader.open). The gate reads the marks in a code file's comments and in a spec's text outside its fenced blocks. Each mark is confronted against the identifiers of the map's code and test files, with their comments removed. A name that is not found fails, naming file:line and the name. A line that cites a name on purpose (one a dependency removed) carries @no-symbol-check: <reason>. Only marked names are read, so an existing project adopts the gate by marking its comments and specs; nothing unmarked is confronted. A mark glued to a word, a path or a link (a#b, /x#y, ](#section)), a name followed by a dash (#css-id), an editor's #region/#endregion, a color (#FFF, #C9BCFF) and the # that opens a comment are not marks. It is in the catalog, informative; declare it with blocking: true to make it block. From MIF: a comment explained a rule by isEvalSupported, an option pdfjs-dist 5 removed, with every gate green. (SYMXS)
Everything in the v0.1.351 notes still applies: run anchors migrate once, crossing format 8.
